[...] ## How This Contract Works

This contract resolves YES if Anthropic’s AI model is judged the best in the industry at year-end 2026. Resolution criteria follow the market’s stated guidelines, likely referencing widely accepted benchmarks, third-party evals, or a panel consensus at close. Every other named company, Google, OpenAI, xAI, Meta, Mistral, Baidu, DeepSeek, Alibaba, Amazon, ByteDance, Microsoft, Moonshot, Meituan, and Z.ai, is a NO outcome for the Anthropic contract.

The NO side pays out when a competitor, most plausibly OpenAI or Google, ships a model that earns the crown before year-end. OpenAI’s next major model release and Google’s Gemini roadmap are the two most obvious catalysts that would push NO into the money.

title: Moonshot AI - Wikipedia
content:
In February 2024, Alibaba Group led a $1 billion funding round for Moonshot, which gave it a valuation of $2.5 billion. Alibaba acquired 36% stake and invested US $0.8 billion in Moonshot AI. Moonshot in January 2026 upgraded its flagship model and now had capabilities that outperformed three of the top U.S. AI models. Alibaba also revealed its latest generative AI model, Qwen3 Max Thinking, which also claimed to have outdone its U.S rivals on a broad benchmark test called 'Humanity's Last Exam.

In August 2024, Tencent and Gaorong Capital joined as investors in a $300 million funding round that valued Moonshot at $3.3 billion. [...] In November 2025, Moonshot released Kimi K2 Thinking, an open-source update to Kimi K2 designed for advanced reasoning and agentic tasks. The model, trained for approximately $4.6 million, features a 1-trillion-parameter MoE architecture with 32 billion active parameters and supports up to 256,000-token contexts. It can execute 200-300 sequential tool calls autonomously and uses native INT4 quantization for efficiency. Benchmarks showed it outperforming GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 on tests including Humanity's Last Exam (44.9%), BrowseComp (60.2%), and SWE-Bench Verified (71.3%). It is released under a modified MIT license requiring attribution for products exceeding 100 million monthly users or $20 million in monthly revenue. [...] In July 2025, the company released the weights for Kimi K2, a large language model with 1 trillion total parameters "Parameter (computer programming)"). The model uses a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture, where 32 billion parameters are active during inference. K2 was trained on 15.5 trillion tokens of data and is released under a modified MIT license. Kimi K2 is an open source LLM, meaning that it can be downloaded and built upon by users. Close watchers of AI have been equally impressed by Moonshot AI’s rapid progress throughout 2025. “K2-Thinking is very close to the frontier,” says Jean-Stanislas Denain, a senior researcher at Epoch AI.

But he cautions against being too focused on AI model benchmarks. “They are meaningful, but capture only a slice of economically relevant capabilities,” says Denain.

Many benchmarks are public, allowing AI labs to target the data they collect to be very similar to the questions asked by benchmark tests. But Hill-Smith notes that Kimi K2 is still “among the leading models in AA-Omniscience”, a new benchmark kept private to avoid manipulation. [...] Independent benchmarking backs up Moonshot AI’s claims. Kimi K2 Thinking scores 66.98 on Artificial Analysis’ Intelligence Index, which tests models’ effectiveness in completing maths, science and coding tasks. This surpassed score of 65.26 for xAI’s Grok 4 and 62.66 for Claude Sonnet 4.5. Kimi K2 has now closed the gap with OpenAI’s GPT-5 and GPT-5.1 models, which respectively scored 68.48 and 69.71.

This marks Moonshot AI’s first model to outperform major Chinese AI labs like Alibaba, DeepSeek, ByteDance and Zhipu. Shanghai-based MiniMax’s M2 model held China’s previous top spot in the intelligence index ranking after it was released on October 26. [...] Kimi K2 Thinking model, released on November 6, is claimed by Moonshot AI to outperform OpenAI’s GPT-5 and Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 4.5 (Thinking) models on several benchmarks. These include Humanity’s Last Exam, which asks expert-level questions on various subjects, and real-world information collection test Seal 0.

Moonshot AI’s latest reasoning model, which is open-source unlike rival proprietary US models, had a more mixed performance in other tests. For instance, it fell just short of GPT-5 and Sonnet 4.5 in the SWE-Bench Verified agentic coding task, according to Moonshot AI’s own analysis.
